summary:
AckerIQ is an open-source orbital agronomy platform that turns NASA Earth-observation data into 4-year climate-resilient crop rotations and cab-ready tractor spreader prescriptions.

Arable farmers face intensifying summer heatwaves, volatile synthetic nitrogen costs, and strict nitrate groundwater caps—yet satellite portals stop at raw raster pixels instead of farm economics or machinery files. Addressing the Field Shift challenge, AckerIQ fuses live NASA POWER (1991–2024 climate shifts, solar irradiance, rainfall), NASA SMAP L4 root-zone soil moisture, Terra MODIS NDVI and land surface temperature, NASA SRTM slope, ISRIC SoilGrids, and Eurostat crop prices for any GPS coordinate or GeoJSON/KML field worldwide.

Using deterministic FAO-56 water-stress, IPCC AR6 N2O, and RUSLE erosion models, AckerIQ ranks drought-safe legume-cereal rotations—cutting synthetic nitrogen up to 82%, curbing nitrate leaching, stacking eco-subsidies, and exporting georeferenced ISO 11783-10 (TASKDATA.XML) variable-rate maps directly to tractor terminals. Live app: https://ackeriq-xwbmhdm34q-ew.a.run.app

7-Slide Technical Deck (PDF): https://github.com/innovpk/ackeriq/blob/main/submission/AckerIQ_NASA_Space_Apps_2026_Slides.pdf

Open-Source Repository (MIT): https://github.com/innovpk/ackeriq

WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

AckerIQ bridges the last-mile gap between coarse satellite rasters and in-cab farm machinery:

1. Parcel & Soil X-Ray: Farmers enter any global GPS coordinate/address, click-draw a field, or drop a .geojson/.kml boundary. AckerIQ queries NASA POWER (1991–2024 climate shifts, solar irradiance, rainfall), NASA SMAP L4 root-zone soil moisture, Terra MODIS 8-day NDVI & daytime LST, NASA SRTM terrain slope, 20 cm DOP20 aerial imagery, and ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 (0–30 cm clay, silt, sand, SOC, pH).

2. Deterministic Agronomy Engine: Peer-reviewed TypeScript models compute FAO-56 evapotranspiration and drought yield response, IPCC 2019/AR6 greenhouse gas flux (GWP100 = 273 for N2O plus winter cover-crop SOC sequestration), and RUSLE hillside soil erosion.

3. 4-Year Rotation & Custom Crop Planner: Ranks phytosanitary-safe legume-cereal rotations, stress-tests 37°C drought summers, evaluates any custom crop against local GDD10/moisture/pH, and stacks live Eurostat €/t crop prices with EU CAP Eco-Scheme 2 & FAKT II subsidies.

4. Direct-to-Tractor Export: Generates georeferenced ISO 11783-10 v4.3 (TASKDATA.XML, DDI 0002) and RFC 7946 GeoJSON variable-rate nitrogen prescriptions for John Deere, Fendt, Amazone, and QGIS.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

On a 165 ha Nitrate-Restricted (Rote Gebiete) benchmark farm over 4 years, AckerIQ's adapted Pea–Spelt–Barley–Soybean rotation delivers:

- 82% less synthetic mineral nitrogen (€102,795 saved via biological N2 fixation & winter catch crops)

- +€246,015 extra 4-year net farm profit (€555/ha/yr vs. €182/ha/yr baseline)

- -783.3 t CO2e net greenhouse gas reduction

- -7,095 kg NO3-N winter groundwater leaching prevented

CREATIVITY & FACTORS CONSIDERED

- Hardware interoperability (converting orbital data into plug-and-play ISOBUS spreader zones)

- Agronomic guardrails (clubroot/legume disease breaks, 7-day rain/wind spreading window compliance)

- Rural usability (bilingual EN/DE interface, zero API keys required, deterministic offline fallbacks for low-signal tractor cabs)

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & ARCHITECTURE

TypeScript, Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, Leaflet 1.9, Recharts 3, and Docker deployed serverless on Google Cloud Run.

SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) ACKNOWLEDGEMENT

SI coding, image, and audio tools (Google Antigravity / Gemini & TTS) assisted with TypeScript/UI scaffolding, bilingual copy, decorative crop/soil card thumbnails, the visibly SI-watermarked story illustrations of Farmer Lukas in our 30-second pitch video, and the video's TTS voiceover narration audio. Zero restricted NASA logos or emblems were used, and 100% of satellite telemetry, agronomic scores, and ISO 11783-10 prescriptions are computed deterministically from public APIs and peer-reviewed physics equations.
